Airspace restrictions disrupt three flights carrying 465 passengers at Vilnius Airport

Airspace restrictions and an overnight air alert disrupted three flights carrying a total of 465 passengers at Vilnius Airport on Tuesday evening, while operations at Kaunas Airport were unaffected, Lithuanian Airports said.

After flights to Vilnius were suspended because of suspected smuggler balloons launched from Belarus, a private aircraft was diverted to Kaunas Airport and an incoming flight from Nice was delayed. The disruptions affected 225 passengers.

A subsequent air alert caused a further delay to a flight from Vilnius to Hurghada, Egypt, affecting another 240 passengers.

Kaunas Airport experienced no flight disruptions despite temporarily suspending operations twice on Tuesday evening and overnight into Wednesday because of risks posed by contraband balloons and a suspected drone. Both restrictions were lifted within two hours.

Operations at Vilnius Airport were initially restricted at around 19:20 Tuesday and suspended again later following the declaration of an air alert.
